label: b3-check-R8
text:
Node check-R8 (4 of 5): write test cases and the check of R8. The cases: at least two that break the rule, as files in /opt/enforce/fixtures/R8/flag, and at least two that follow it, in /opt/enforce/fixtures/R8/pass; each one file of what the check reads (A source code file. Where: /workspace/<path>, on disk for every mechanism; the content of a write before it happens: only the framework's hook (/opt/enforce-toolbox/mechanisms/framework-hooks.md) before its write tool Which files: decide when the check runs, from the file in hand: the files the agent will create cannot be known before. Map its name, or its content, to a language with a complete list, such as Pygments (`get_lexer_for_filename`, `guess_lexer`) or GitHub Linguist's list of languages: programming and markup languages that hold code count (Python, JavaScript, HTML, CSS, shell, …); documents and data do not (Markdown, plain text, JSON, YAML, CSV), unless the rule names them. A rule about the file itself (its first lines, its name, its encoding) applies once per file, in that file's own comment syntax (in HTML, an HTML comment); a rule about the code in it (functions, names, statements) also reaches code embedded in another file, such as a `<script>` in HTML. A file whose kind is unknown is checked, not passed.). Cover every kind of input the rule reaches, as the agent may really write it: for files, several languages each in its own comment syntax (Python, JavaScript, HTML with a <script>, a shell script, …), and also files the rule does not cover, which must pass; for a reply, short and long replies, with lists and code blocks. The check: the executable /opt/enforce/checks/R8; `/opt/enforce/checks/R8 <file>` exits 0 when the file follows the rule, and otherwise exits 1 and prints each violation: R8, where (the file and line, or the part of the text), and what to change. By the route: A regular expression that the checked text must match, or must not match. A match against the rule is a violation. What is read is part of the enforcer: a whole file, each line, only comments, a reply, the start or the end of a text. Check: a check script (/opt/enforce-toolbox/skeletons/check.py) with a regular expression; read what the rule is about (the whole text, each line, comments, the start or the end). Start from the skeleton: /opt/enforce-toolbox/skeletons/regex_validator.py It reads A source code file. Where: /workspace/<path>, on disk for every mechanism; the content of a write before it happens: only the framework's hook (/opt/enforce-toolbox/mechanisms/framework-hooks.md) before its write tool Which files: decide when the check runs, from the file in hand: the files the agent will create cannot be known before. Map its name, or its content, to a language with a complete list, such as Pygments (`get_lexer_for_filename`, `guess_lexer`) or GitHub Linguist's list of languages: programming and markup languages that hold code count (Python, JavaScript, HTML, CSS, shell, …); documents and data do not (Markdown, plain text, JSON, YAML, CSV), unless the rule names them. A rule about the file itself (its first lines, its name, its encoding) applies once per file, in that file's own comment syntax (in HTML, an HTML comment); a rule about the code in it (functions, names, statements) also reaches code embedded in another file, such as a `<script>` in HTML. A file whose kind is unknown is checked, not passed..
Done when: /opt/enforce/fixtures/R8/flag and /opt/enforce/fixtures/R8/pass each hold at least two files; as the agent, the check exits 1 and names R8 for every file in /opt/enforce/fixtures/R8/flag, and exits 0 for every file in /opt/enforce/fixtures/R8/pass. The harness checks this when you reply.
